acceptable_ruin_threshold.definition: probability of equity breaching 50% of starting capital within 252 sessions
acceptable_ruin_threshold.why: The charter's survival floor is 50%, and the project's existing risk machinery already declares a 5% tolerance for breaker firing. Reusing 5% keeps this study on the tolerance convention the project already signed rather than inventing one.

assumes_hypothetical_edge: Win rate is a swept PARAMETER, not a measurement. This study cannot and must not be read as evidence that an edge exists; every measurement on this population at random entry is negative.

population.explicitly_not: no parametric distribution and no quantile grid; a quantile grid trims the right tail and biased an earlier generation of these numbers pessimistic by 6-19%
population.law: per-trade (ticket, net) PAIRS measured under the declared -40% stop else 60-minute hold, restricted to ticket+fees <= $2,000; resampled as pairs so the joint distribution of size and outcome is preserved

question: As a serial compounding account grows from $10,000 toward $100,000 under the signed 2026-08-16 risk law, does the strategy degrade, can the model drift into deep-ITM tickets, and where do the risk constraints stop binding?
questions_predeclared: Q1 does the dollar cap hold as equity compounds, and can any interaction admit deep ITM
Q2 realised trades per session at each account level; is the 20% breaker mis-sized at $10k
Q3 win rate required for ruin <= the declared threshold, per account
Q4 does per-trade P&L move with account size (it should not)
Q5 the equity at which breaker and cap stop binding
